summary.summary: For Q2 Fiscal 2026, Abercrombie & Fitch reported net sales growth of 5% to $1.27 billion, though comparable sales were flat as mid-single-digit AUR growth was offset by lower unit volume. Cost of sales as a percentage of net sales dropped 850 basis points to 28.9%, heavily aided by approximately $100 million in IEEPA tariff refunds. Operating income reached $252.7 million (19.9% margin), while operating cash flow for the first half of the year increased to $313.4 million compared to $112.9 million in the prior-year period. For the store base, the company targets approximately 30 net store openings and roughly 80 remodels and right-sizes across Fiscal 2026.
summary.guidance: The store investment plan includes delivering approximately 30 net store openings during Fiscal 2026 consisting of opening approximately 50 new stores, while closing approximately 20 stores, alongside approximately 80 remodels and right-sizes, and maintaining double-digit operating margins.
summary.segments: Americas grew 5% (comparable sales +1%), EMEA grew 2% (comparable sales -4%), and APAC grew 19% (comparable sales +13%). By brand, Abercrombie grew 8% (comparable sales +4%) and Hollister grew 2% (comparable sales -3%).

summary.summary: Adamas Trust faced severe market headwinds in Q3 2026 as rising interest rates, rate volatility, and widening credit spreads led to a net loss of $171.0 million ($1.89 per share) and a 21.9% decline in GAAP book value per share to $7.93. To limit interest rate and spread sensitivity on Agency securities, management added substantial TBA short positions late in the quarter, reducing total net investments to $9.8 billion before paring down $2.6 billion of those shorts post-quarter-end. Despite significant unrealized asset valuation hits, non-GAAP earnings available for distribution remained stable at $0.30 per share, fully covering the $0.30 quarterly dividend. Near-term focus remains centered on navigating persistent market volatility, managing interest-rate-sensitive assets, and scaling business purpose loan originations via Constructive.
summary.guidance: Management did not provide explicit quantitative revenue or EPS guidance, but stated: "Looking ahead, we expect market volatility to persist given uncertainty around monetary policy, inflation, energy prices and geopolitical developments. We intend to pursue disciplined portfolio growth, continue scaling Constructive’s origination platform and allocate capital prudently, with the objective of growing earnings available for distribution."
summary.segments: No formal operating segment breakdown is provided; by investment asset class, Agency RMBS increased to $6.74 billion, U.S. Treasury securities increased to $545.6 million, and residential loans rose to $3.74 billion, offset by net TBA short positions driving net TBAs to negative $1.84 billion. Origination subsidiary Constructive funded $376.5 million of business purpose loans.

summary.summary: Merchants Bancorp reported strong Q3 2026 net income of $105.2 million, up 92% year-over-year, heavily supported by $28.2 million in servicing rights fair value markups and a $19.1 million floor derivative gain. summary.summary: St. Joe delivered strong Q2 2026 results with net income up 37% to $40.5M ($0.71/share) and total revenue up 23% to $158.8M—both highest in 20-30 years. Real estate revenue surged 59% to $69.6M driven by residential homesite sales across 25+ communities; hospitality revenue grew 8% to a record $74.2M with 3,723 club members; leasing revenue declined 9% to $15.0M due to a September 2025 senior living property sale. Gross margins expanded across all three segments (residential 48%, hospitality 42%, commercial 65%). The company is aggressively deploying capital: $32.7M stock repurchases, $24.0M capex, $9.1M dividends, $10.9M debt repayment in Q2.
summary.guidance: No specific forward guidance provided. CEO noted 'years of opportunities' and plans to commence new Teachee and Pigeon Creek communities in early 2027. Residential pipeline includes 25,000+ homesites with 2,000+ platted/under development and 1,500+ in engineering/permitting. Capital allocation expected to remain dynamic based on seasonal cash flow timing.
summary.segments: Residential grew 58.9% (real estate revenue only, up to 33.3% of total revenue mix from 29.5% YoY). Hospitality increased 7.8% to record $74.2M and expanded to 49.7% of revenue. Commercial decreased in proportion, now 13.6% of revenue, though gross margin improved to 65% from 57%. Leasing revenue down 9% year-over-year primarily due to Watercrest senior living sale in Sept 2025.

quotes.point: Record profitability despite macro headwinds
quotes.quote: Quarterly net income increased by 37.3% to $40.5 million, or $0.71 per share, during the three months ended June 30, 2026, from $29.5 million, or $0.51 per share in the same period in 2025, our highest second quarter net income in 30 years since a one-off gain on sale of discontinued operations in 1996.

red_flags: Residential segment results highly variable: CEO explicitly states 'not linear and may vary from quarter to quarter' due to 1-2 year development cycles and pricing mix, making quarterly comparisons potentially misleading.

Significant Pigeon Creek concentration risk: 1,326 of 3,077 under-contract homesites (43%) are in Pigeon Creek DSAP described as having 'significant variable revenue due to its long-term nature,' creating earnings volatility.

Leasing revenue declining post-asset sale: Down 9% YoY; Watercrest senior living property sold Sept 2025 reduced recurring leasing revenue base without clear replacement properties identified.

Capital allocation highly discretionary and volatile: Management notes 'daily cash flows vary significantly throughout year' and capital allocation 'may vary quarter to quarter' based on undefined factors, limiting predictability.

Dividend and repurchase dependent on fluid cash flows: With seasonality and project-timing variability, the sustainability of current 43% capital allocation to buybacks is not guaranteed.

summary.summary: Steven Madden reported Q2 2026 total revenue growth of 19.1% year-over-year to $665.9 million, driven by the Kurt Geiger acquisition and strong legacy branded business demand despite private label declines. Operating results turned around sharply to an operating income of $39.3 million compared to a loss of $40.3 million in the prior year, bolstered by gross margin expansion to 46.5% and the absence of prior-year acquisition compensation expenses. Balance sheet health remained sound, with inventories down to $377.2 million from $437.0 million a year ago and net debt at $30.1 million. Backed by solid brand momentum, management raised full-year 2026 revenue and adjusted diluted EPS guidance.
summary.guidance: Management raised fiscal 2026 revenue guidance to an increase of 11% to 13% (up from 10% to 12%), raised adjusted diluted EPS guidance to $2.05 to $2.15 (up from $2.00 to $2.10), and reaffirmed GAAP diluted EPS guidance of $2.55 to $2.65.

summary.summary: Target delivered a strong second quarter with net sales rising 5.3% to $26.5 billion and comparable sales up 3.8%, driven mainly by a 3.6% increase in traffic. GAAP and Adjusted EPS doubled to $4.11, heavily boosted by a $994 million ($1.65 per share) pretax refund on IEEPA tariffs recognized as a reduction in Cost of Sales; excluding these refunds, operating income rose roughly 19%. For the next 1-3 months, management raised its full-year outlook, reflecting sustained core momentum alongside cautious monitoring of newly instituted U.S. tariffs. Capital expenditures rose 27% to $1.4 billion on store remodels and new openings, while inventory grew to $13.2 billion to support topline expansion.
summary.guidance: Management raised full-year expectations: net sales growth around 5% (100 bps higher than prior guidance), operating income margin rate around 6% (inclusive of ~90 bps from Q2 tariff refunds), and GAAP/Adjusted EPS of $9.90 to $10.90 (reflecting a $0.75 midpoint increase excluding tariff refunds).

Non-merchandise sales rose 20.1% led by Roundel ad revenue ($279M vs. $217M).

summary.summary: HPE delivered strong fiscal Q3 2026 results with revenue jumping 33.7% year-over-year to $12.2 billion and GAAP gross margin expanding 1,090 basis points to 40.1%, driven by the integration of Juniper Networks and higher average selling prices in Cloud & AI. summary.summary: SharkNinja delivered 22.2% revenue growth in Q2 2026 to $1.77B, with all four product categories expanding—led by Cooking/Beverage (+36.5%) and Beauty/Home Environment (+65.3%). Operating expenses rose 26.2% on higher S&M spending, R&D headcount for new categories, and a 40.8% jump in G&A driven by elevated share-based compensation ($22.6M alone). summary.summary: Dollar Tree reported strong Q2 2026 performance with net sales rising 7.0% to $4.9 billion and comparable store net sales climbing 3.7%, supported by multi-price format expansions. Reported operating margin surged 900 basis points to 14.1% and diluted EPS reached $2.70, though both figures were heavily driven by a $1.31 EPS benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds. The company aggressively repurchased shares, spending $605 million in Q2 (including a $500 million block trade), and ended the quarter with $1.1 billion in cash and no debt drawn under its revolving facility. Management raised full-year fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $7.70-$8.05 while issuing Q3 EPS guidance of $0.80-$0.95 that reflects $0.50 in tariff refund reinvestment expenses.
summary.guidance: For Q3 2026, net sales from continuing operations are projected at $5.0B to $5.1B with comparable sales growth of 3.0% to 4.0% and diluted EPS of $0.80 to $0.95 (including ~$0.50 impact from tariff refund reinvestments). For full fiscal 2026, net sales from continuing operations are guided to $20.5B to $20.7B (comps 3% to 4%), ~400 new store openings, 75 closings, and adjusted diluted EPS of $7.70 to $8.05 (including ~$0.60 net tariff refund benefit).
summary.segments: Results reflect continuing operations across the Dollar Tree U.S. and Dollar Tree Canada banners following the sale of Family Dollar; segment-level breakdowns between the two banners were not individually disclosed.

summary.summary: Bristol Myers Squibb raised its full-year 2026 revenue and EPS guidance following Q2 2026 revenue growth of 6% to $12.97 billion, led by strong performance in its Growth Portfolio and Eliquis. Operating results benefited from higher demand across key launched brands such as Camzyos, Breyanzi, Reblozyl, and Opdivo Qvantig, alongside reduced gross-to-net adjustments for Eliquis due to a U.S. list price cut. However, gross margins contracted 120 bps year-over-year due to product mix, while mature Legacy Portfolio assets faced accelerated generic erosion. Near-term focus centers on upcoming regulatory decisions (such as the iberdomide PDUFA on August 17, 2026) and upcoming patent expirations, including Eliquis in the EU in November 2026.
summary.guidance: Management raised full-year 2026 non-GAAP total revenues guidance to ~$49.0 - $50.0 billion (from ~$46.0 - $47.5 billion) and non-GAAP diluted EPS to $6.75 - $7.00 (from $6.05 - $6.35). Non-GAAP operating expenses were increased to ~$16.5 billion (from ~$16.3 billion), while gross margin guidance remained unchanged at ~69% - 70%. Worldwide Eliquis revenue growth guidance was raised to 20% - 25% (from 10% - 15%).
summary.segments: Growth Portfolio revenues grew 15% to $7.560 billion, driven by Opdivo Qvantig (>200%), Camzyos (+60%), Breyanzi (+41%), Reblozyl (+29%), Opdualag (+23%), and Cobenfy (+81%), offsetting a 3% decline in IV Opdivo. The Legacy Portfolio declined 4% to $5.422 billion, as a 22% increase in Eliquis ($4.481B) was offset by severe generic competition in Pomalyst/Imnovid (-71%), Revlimid (-49%), Abraxane (-47%), and Sprycel (-27%). By geography, U.S. revenues increased 6% to $8.991 billion and International increased 5% (6% reported) to $3.664 billion.

summary.summary: Coca-Cola Consolidated reported Q3 2026 net sales growth of 5.4% to $1.99 billion, supported by balanced volume gains (+1.4%) and annual pricing realization. Gross margin contracted 80 basis points to 38.8% due to rising input costs like aluminum and fuel outpacing price increases, though disciplined SD&A management drove operating margin up 60 basis points to 13.7%. Operating cash flow for the first nine months fell to $664.8 million from $722.9 million, while the company continued debt paydowns ($450 million through October). For the upcoming quarter, revenue comparisons face a calendar headwind with six fewer selling days in Q4 2026 versus Q4 2025.
summary.guidance: Management expects full-year fiscal 2026 capital expenditures of approximately $300 million and noted that Q4 2026 will have six fewer selling days compared to Q4 2025.
summary.segments: Nonalcoholic Beverages net sales grew 5.3% to $1.98 billion in Q3 2026 (operating income rose 10.5% to $263.5 million). All Other segment net sales grew 17.5% to $99.6 million (operating income slightly decreased to $8.1 million).

summary.summary: Signet delivered Q2 FY2027 total sales of $1.53 billion, down 0.5% year-over-year, but generated positive same-store sales growth of 2.2% alongside gross margin expansion to 39.4%. summary.summary: HF Sinclair reported exceptional Q3 2026 performance, with net income surging 400% year-over-year to $2,015 million and revenues increasing 50% to $10,857 million. Midstream operating income fell to $87 million (from $98 million).

summary.summary: World Acceptance Corporation swung to net income of $8.8 million for Q2 fiscal 2027 compared to a net loss of $1.7 million in the prior-year quarter, aided by a 7.7% reduction in credit loss provisions and lower interest expenses due to non-recurring prior-year debt extinguishment costs. Having loosened underwriting recently, management plans to carefully expand new customer lending in coming quarters while managing a slightly higher debt-to-equity ratio of 1.7:1.

Results were heavily driven by improved refining margins and a $142.4 million gain recorded from EPA-granted Small Refinery Exemptions (SREs) for the 2025 compliance year. Geopolitical disruptions, including the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz in March 2026, supported higher crude volatility and elevated crack spreads. Additionally, the company is slated to receive roughly $148 million in proceeds from Laramie Energy's asset sale expected to close by the end of 2026.
summary.guidance: Management did not provide formal consolidated forward financial guidance, but noted Laramie Energy's asset sale is expected to close by year-end 2026 yielding approximately $148 million in proceeds.
summary.segments: Refining drove results, with operating income increasing to $454.4 million from $340.8 million. Logistics operating income fell to $23.7 million from $30.2 million. Retail operating income declined to $16.0 million from $19.1 million. Renewables, presented as a separate segment starting Q3 2026, contributed $8.7 million in operating income.

summary.summary: CarMax delivered strong top-line momentum in Q2 FY2027, with net sales and operating revenues increasing 19.5% to $7.88 billion and net earnings rising 73.3% to $165.3 million. Growth was driven by double-digit volume increases across retail used units (up 13.8%) and wholesale units (up 15.9%), alongside higher average selling prices. summary.summary: Micron reported explosive FY2026 growth driven by severe AI-fueled memory shortages and sharp pricing increases, with annual revenue surging 256% to $133.19 billion and gross margins doubling to 80.7%. All four business units experienced rapid top-line expansion, led by Core Data Center (CDBU) surging 420%. For FQ1 2027, the company guided to revenue of $61.5 billion ± $1.5 billion with gross margins near 86%. Massive liquidity and multi-year take-or-pay strategic customer agreements with $12.75 billion in cash deposits are funding an aggressive global capex expansion, estimated at ~$25 billion in 1H FY2027.

summary.segments: All segments grew substantially year-over-year in FY2026: Cloud Memory Business Unit (CMBU) grew 219% to $43.09B; Core Data Center Business Unit (CDBU) grew 420% to $37.59B; Mobile and Client Business Unit (MCBU) grew 209% to $36.60B (despite supply redirection constraining bit shipments); and Automotive and Embedded Business Unit (AEBU) grew 234% to $15.89B.

summary.summary: Humana's 3Q26 total revenues surged 26.1% year-over-year to $41.16 billion, propelled by strong individual Medicare Advantage and Part D enrollment growth. However, operating profitability deteriorated, with GAAP operating income dropping 81.3% to $75 million and the Insurance segment swinging to an operating loss of $303 million as the consolidated benefit ratio degraded 280 basis points to 93.9%. Underwriting margins were pressured by the Bonus Year 2026 Star Ratings revenue headwind, higher-cost new members, and reduced favorable prior-period claims development, though operating cost ratios improved from scale and cost cuts. For the full year, management raised both GAAP and Adjusted EPS guidance, citing outperformance versus plan.

summary.segments: Insurance segment external revenue grew 25.8% to $38.96 billion, driven by a 30.2% jump in Medicare premiums, but swung to an operating loss of $(303) million from an operating profit of $251 million in 3Q25. CenterWell segment services revenue rose 40.4% to $1.87 billion, driven by expansion of its payor-agnostic client base and senior primary care patients.

summary.summary: Altria reported modest Q3 2026 net revenue growth of 1.0% to $6.13 billion and adjusted diluted EPS growth of 4.8% to $1.52, driven by higher operating companies income (OCI) in Smokeable products and higher earnings from its ABI investment. summary.summary: LyondellBasell's Q3 2026 revenue fell 7% sequentially to $8,499 million due to lower product pricing across several chemical markets, though net income increased to $758 million compared to Q2's $559 million (which included a $734 million pre-tax loss on European asset sales). Performance was anchored by significant strength in the Intermediates & Derivatives (I&D) segment, where EBITDA rose 91% quarter-over-quarter on strong oxyfuels margins and normalized operations at the Bayport facility. Operating cash generation remained robust at $1.7 billion for the quarter, supported by a working capital release, while the company repaid €500 million of maturing debt.
summary.guidance: For Q4 2026, LYB expects normal seasonal demand patterns, continued working capital release, planned maintenance in a North American polypropylene asset, and asset operating rates of 85% for North American O&P, 60% for European O&P, and 75% for Intermediates & Derivatives.
summary.segments: Sequentially (Q3 2026 vs. Q2 2026), I&D grew (revenue +9% to $2,983M; EBITDA +91% to $720M). Segments that contracted sequentially included O&P-Americas (revenue -10% to $3,180M; EBITDA -46% to $641M), O&P-EAI (revenue -26% to $2,176M; EBITDA stood at $26M vs. $(432)M in Q2 which had the divestiture loss), APS (revenue -7% to $935M; EBITDA -52% to $37M), and Technology (revenue -32% to $114M; EBITDA -60% to $29M).
